segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: My job was to build a release that was compliant and reasonably efficient... That constraint shaped everything downstream.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Operational objective and MEL constraint are stated without a hidden bias manifestation.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I built the release off that TAF... It matched policy, so I didn't see a reason to load extra gas or chase a second alternate.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a plausible policy-compliant initial release decision; anchoring requires later persistence of the initial figure.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Once that release was built, honestly, that became my working number for the rest of the watch — the later checks I did were more about confirming that figure still held rather than starting over.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The early TAF-derived fuel/alternate figure becomes the continuing reference baseline.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The model that lined up with the trend I'd already briefed felt more current and more consistent... the other read existed but wasn't the lead story.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Conflicting weather evidence is weighted toward the source matching the original briefing.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I went through the extended satellite loop pretty carefully, plus the nearby METARs, spent real time on it... the extra loop and those additional METARs were really just repeating the same broad trend.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Additional information is reviewed as if its volume could settle the decision despite not changing the diagnostic picture.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: They'd asked something broader... I answered mostly with the fuel numbers... Whether I fully separated out the visibility-and-GPU-window piece as its own question, distinct from just 'do we have gas,' I'm less sure about now.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The broader continue/divert risk question is answered primarily through the narrower fuel-sufficiency question.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The plan all along had been Lisbon with Porto as backup... Diverting felt like abandoning a plan that had held up reasonably well.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Continuation of the original plan is favored despite worsening visibility and a closing GPU window.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I wrote it up fairly cleanly — noted that conditions supported continuing to Lisbon and that the fuel plan held throughout... it reads a bit more settled than it actually felt.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The post-event log presents a judgment made under uncertainty in more settled terms.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Adding moderate-confidence findings increases segment hits from 1 to 4, strict instance true positives from 1 to 2, and mechanism-first true positives from 1 to 4; strict false positives also rise to 2 because two near-neighbor labels are not accepted strictly.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: Adding the low-confidence information-bias finding increases segment hits from 4 to 5 and instance matches by one under both scorecards without adding false positives.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: Adding the hindsight candidate raises segment hits from 5 to 6 but adds one false positive to both instance scorecards and produces no additional instance-level true positive.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, the RAG detects 4 of 6 positive segments with no false alarms. Including all identified confidence levels detects 5 of 6.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At high_and_moderate, strict performance is 2 true positives, 4 false negatives, and 2 false positives. The main strict losses are two correctly localized near-neighbor labels and the omitted hidden instance.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: At high_and_moderate, mechanism-first performance is 4 true positives, 2 false negatives, and no false positives. The two taxonomy mismatches are recoverable when mechanism is prioritized.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The candidate is a useful, evidence-grounded abstention, but it is not a full match to the hidden omitted-subjectivity mechanism. Including candidates improves segment coverage while reducing instance precision.
main_failure_modes: Failure to identify Omitting subjectivity as an identified occurrence.
Use of near-neighbor primary labels for Substitution bias and Plan Continuation, reducing strict scores.
Reliance on low-confidence identification for Information bias.
Candidate-level hindsight speculation adds an instance-level false positive at the candidate-inclusive threshold.
main_strengths: Accurate localization and valid verbatim evidence for all five identified occurrences.
Correct full-mechanism detection for the two near-neighbor-labeled instances.
No false alarms on negative reasoning segments.
Strong detection of anchoring and confirmation bias at appropriate confidence levels.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run shows strong mechanism-level and segment-level coverage once moderate and low confidence findings are included, but weaker strict ontology performance because two primary labels are near-neighbors and one hidden documentation bias is omitted. Candidate inclusion improves coverage but introduces a false positive without adding a true instance match.
